topic: Nilsson et al. 2006, C5-BTBP extraction properties (SEIX 24(3) 299-318, DOI 10.1080/07366290600646947): how D was measured, any detection floor for light lanthanides, open-access copies, and whether the 15 corpus cells really come from this paper

findings.question: Q1/Q3: Can the paper's full text be read, and what does the paper itself say about how D was measured?
findings.statement: The publisher full text returned HTTP 403 (paywalled). OpenAlex marks the paper oa_status 'closed', with no open-access URL and no repository full text. Semantic Scholar shows openAccessPdf as empty and notes the publisher withheld the abstract. Crossref confirms the bibliographic data: vol. 24, issue 3, pp. 299-318, nine authors. Because the full text could not be read, no statement from the paper about tracers, ICP-MS or isotopes could be checked.
findings.consequence: We have no source-verified measurement method or detection limit from the paper itself. Any floor or censoring treatment for these 15 cells stays an assumption until someone with journal access reads the Experimental section.

findings.question: Q1: What does the paper's own abstract cover (metals, diluents)?
findings.statement: Abstract rebuilt word for word from OpenAlex's abstract_inverted_index. It covers only Am(III) and Eu(III) into 'a variety of organic diluents'. It also covers stoichiometry, contact time, temperature, gamma resistance and recycling. Results range from no extraction to D(Am) > 1000; in 1,1,2,2-tetrachloroethane SF(Am/Eu) > 60 at about 5 min. D(Am) falls about 80% after 17 kGy. The abstract names no lanthanide series and no kerosene/octanol mixture. Quote: 'ranging from no extraction to distribution ratios over 1000 for americium(III)'.
findings.consequence: Our corpus has 15 cells under this DOI: 13 lanthanides (La-Lu without Pm and Tm), in 70% kerosene / 30% 1-octanol, at 0.1-1.0 M HNO3, with 0.005/0.01/0.015 M C5-BTBP, at 20 C, curator Baosen Zhang, data_location empty. The abstract describes none of this, so the attribution of these cells is doubtful and should be checked against the full text before any floor treatment is applied.

findings.question: Provenance: could the 15 kerosene/octanol lanthanide cells come from Foreman et al. 2005 instead?
findings.statement: Foreman, Hudson, Geist, Madic and Weigl 2005, SEIX 23(5) 645-662, DOI 10.1080/07366290500230735. The title covers 'Americium(III), Lanthanides and D-Block Metals' with C5-BTBP. The abstract (OpenAlex) says: 'In octanol/kerosene the distribution ratios suggest that stripping will be possible.' Separately, the Crossref reference list deposited for Nilsson 2006 (31 references) does not include the Foreman 2005 DOI.
findings.consequence: This is only a hypothesis, not a verified attribution. The diluent and metal list fit Foreman 2005 better than Nilsson 2006. Foreman 2005 is also closed access (Reading repository record has no full text). If the cells belong to Foreman 2005, the measurement method and detection limit are unknown and the copy-group/source-cluster logic should be revisited.

findings.question: Q1 (same group's report): how did Chalmers measure D in its C5-BTBP work?
findings.statement: SKB report R-05-13, Partitioning and Transmutation Annual Report 2004, by Andersson, Drouet, Ekberg, Liljenzin, Magnusson, Nilsson, Retegan, Skarnemark (Jan 2005, open PDF). Section 2.1 'Chemical behaviour of C5-BTBP' describes trace experiments with 241Am and 152Eu measured by gamma spectroscopy. In the macro-Ln runs (0.01 M C5 + 0.25 M 2-bromohexanoic acid in TBB), 241Am/244Cm/252Cf were measured by alpha spectroscopy and lanthanides by ICP-MS. Quote: 'ICP-MS analysis for inactive lanthanides (La, Ce, Pr, Nd, Sm, Eu, Gd) and Y'.
findings.consequence: This is the best open evidence on the group's methods: radiotracer gamma/alpha for Am/Eu/Cm/Cf, ICP-MS for inactive Ln. The listed ICP-MS elements stop at Gd, while the corpus cells include Tb-Lu. It does not establish which method produced the 15 corpus cells.

findings.question: Q2: Does the same group state a lowest measurable D or 'no extraction' threshold for C5-BTBP?
findings.statement: R-05-13, diluent screening: 0.005 M C5 in each diluent, 0.01 M H+ / 1 M NO3-, trace 241Am or 152Eu, triplicates. It reports that hexane and TPH could not dissolve C5, and that trichloroethylene gave no extraction, stated as D < 10^-4. Quote: 'no extraction (D<10–4) was observed for neither americium nor europium'.
findings.consequence: This is the group's own operational floor for radiotracer D: below 1e-4 is reported as 'no extraction', and the paper's abstract also uses the phrase 'no extraction'. The corpus La median log D is -4.24, at or below log D = -4. This supports treating these values as censored or near-floor, but it is not a source-verified detection limit for the corpus cells. It applies to a different diluent and probably a different method (tracer, not ICP-MS).

findings.question: Q2: Does the same group's report say C5-BTBP dissolves in aliphatic diluents?
findings.statement: R-05-13 says that of hexane, TPH and trichloroethylene, C5 could not be dissolved in the first two (0.005 M). It also says that in 1-alcohols (hexanol to decanol), longer chains gave lower extraction and lower separation, which it calls bad news for kerosene-type process diluents. No C5-BTBP data in kerosene/octanol mixtures appear in the 2004 report.
findings.consequence: Chalmers' 2004 programme, which appears to underlie Nilsson 2006, has no 70/30 kerosene/octanol experiments. This weakens the attribution of the 15 corpus cells to this DOI.

findings.question: Q2: Any statement that low lanthanide D values were hard to measure in the group's related C5-BTBP work?
findings.statement: R-05-13, C5 in cyclohexanone with a HAW-type solution: Ln values are from a single sample, so uncertainties could not be calculated. Quote: 'the heaviest lanthanides were present only in small amounts in the initial aqueous solutions'. The same report, for a different ligand (BODO, HPGe tracer measurements), says Tb, Tm, Yb and Lu could not be evaluated because of low D and/or difficulties in evaluating the spectra.
findings.consequence: This is qualitative evidence that the lab's Ln measurements lose precision at low concentration or low D. The cyclohexanone passage is relevant to the companion paper DOI 10.1080/07366290600952659 (pub_723ceb6c2c, 1 corpus cell). No numeric limit is given.

findings.question: Q2: Does the 2005 annual report mention a detection limit?
findings.statement: SKB R-06-45, Partitioning and Transmutation Annual Report 2005 (Chalmers, Jan 2006). For CyMe4-S-BTP in tetrachloroethane, it says the 152Eu D is 'uncertain since it is close to the detection limit'. No number is given. The report also lists Nilsson et al. C5-BTBP as 'Accepted for publication in Solvent Extraction and Ion Exchange 2006', and says Nilsson defended his PhD in December 2005.
findings.consequence: This confirms the group's tracer D measurements had a practical detection limit, but it is for a different ligand and gives no value. It does not change the dataset directly.

findings.question: Q3: Thesis versions (Nilsson, Andersson) with open full text?
findings.statement: Mikael Nilsson, 'Screening Investigations of Novel Nitrogen Donor Ligands', Chalmers doctoral thesis 2005 (ISBN 91-7291-699-0; keywords include BTBP). The Chalmers record (publication 8594) shows only the abstract, with no PDF or list of appended papers; OpenAlex marks it closed. Sofie Andersson's 2005 thesis is on other systems (BODO/2-bromodecanoic acid, nitrate complexes), not C5-BTBP extraction, per its Chalmers record and the search snippet.
findings.consequence: There is no open thesis copy that would expose the paper's Experimental section. A Chalmers library request (the record points to research.lib@chalmers.se) is the only route found.

findings.question: Q3: Any other open-access copy (institutional repository, OSTI, ResearchGate, CORE)?
findings.statement: Chalmers research record 25110 lists bibliographic data only, with no abstract or full text. ResearchGate and Academia.edu returned 403. CORE and scholar.archive.org showed bot-check pages, and the Reading CentAUR record showed an Anubis bot check. None was bypassed. No OSTI or EUROPART deliverable with C5-BTBP lanthanide D values or detection limits turned up in searches.
findings.consequence: No open-access copy exists among the sources checked. The open SKB annual reports (R-05-13, R-06-45) are the only related public material.

Its abstract, rebuilt word for word from OpenAlex, covers only Am(III) and Eu(III) in 'a variety of organic diluents'. It mentions no lanthanide series and no kerosene/octanol mixture. A separate passage also mentions a detection limit. It concerns ICP-MS work in Tables 2-15 and 2-16, where a dash marks results "either below the detection limit" or doubtful in analysis. Some of those results are based on single samples. That passage gives no number either.

(2) The publication list includes: M. Nilsson, S. Andersson, F. Drouet et al., "Extraction Properties of 6,6'-bis-(5,6-dipentyl-[1,2,4]triazin-3-yl)-[2,2']bipyridinyl (C5-BTBP)". It is marked "Accepted for publication in Solvent Extraction and Ion Exchange 2006."

(3) Section 2, Research, says Sofie Andersson and Mikael Nilsson "defended their theses", Andersson in April and Nilsson in December (2005).

Answer to Q2: yes, the report mentions a detection limit only in words, never as a number.

topic: Shimada, Yaita, Narita, Tachimori, Okuno 2004, SEIX 22(2) 147-161, DOI 10.1081/SEI-120030392 (DMDPhPDA/CHCl3, Ln(III) from 1-5 M HNO3): public evidence for Pr/Nd D at 5 M HNO3 and SF along the series

findings.question: (1) Are Table 1 / Fig. 5 (Pr, Nd D at 5 M HNO3) readable on the abstract page?
findings.statement: The T&F abstract page returned HTTP 403. OpenAlex reproduces the publisher abstract: D of lanthanides measured from 1 to 5 M HNO3 into DMDPhPDA/CHCl3, and the number of ligands per extracted complex rises from 3 for light Ln to 4 for heavy Ln. The abstract also says acid concentration matters more than ligand concentration for D 'and the difference of distribution ratio among lanthanides'. The abstract gives no numeric D values, no SF, and does not mention Pr or Nd. Crossref has no abstract (28 references). OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar both mark the paper closed access with no OA copy.
findings.consequence: The abstract cannot settle the one-decade discrepancy. Its only use is qualitative: inter-Ln differences depend mainly on acid concentration, which is the axis where the two corpus copies disagree. The full text is paywalled and was not read.

findings.question: (1) Is there a public full-text source (thesis/report) likely to contain the Table 1 / Fig. 5 values?
findings.statement: Asako Shimada's doctoral thesis, Shizuoka University, 2004-03-23, in Japanese. Title: '3価アクチノイドに対する抽出剤の開発とその抽出機構の解明' (development of extractants for trivalent actinides and their extraction mechanism). Degree 博士(理学) 甲第379号, DOI 10.14945/00003509. The repository lists one attached file, K0379.pdf (23.8 MB), marked open access. I did NOT download or read it, because the task rules forbid saving files to disk, so its contents are unverified. It plausibly holds the DMDPhPDA Ln D tables, since it shares the author and year with the SEIX paper.
findings.consequence: This is the most promising public route to the original D values for Pr and Nd at 5 M HNO3, and it could arbitrate between the curated and ORNL copies. Reading it needs explicit user permission to download a 23.8 MB PDF from shizuoka.repo.nii.ac.jp. The file may be a scan, in which case OCR would be needed.

findings.question: (1)/(3) Conference proceeding with this system's acid dependence along the series
findings.statement: AESJ 2003 fall meeting abstract (Shimada, Yaita, Okuno, Kimura; DOI 10.11561/aesj.2003f.0.460.0), in Japanese. Ln D vs [HNO3] has a slope near 3 up to about 3 M. Above 3 M, D rises sharply, 'especially for heavy Ln' (translated). A run at a fixed 4 M nitrate (HNO3 + LiNO3) also points to HNO3 molecules taking part in extraction. No numeric D, no SF, no Pr or Nd, no 5 M value.
findings.consequence: Above 3 M HNO3 the D values change steeply and differ by Ln, so a one-decade slip at 5 M is chemically plausible in either direction. The abstract confirms the regime is non-linear but does not say which copy is right.

findings.question: (1)/(2) Companion paper by the same group restating Ln D values
findings.statement: A companion paper exists: Shimada, Yaita, Narita et al., 'Extraction of Am(III) and Lanthanide(III) Ions from HNO3 Solutions Using DMDPhPDA'. It is in Solvent Extraction Research and Development, Japan, vol. 11 (2004), pp. 1-10, and is recorded in NDL and CiNii. J-STAGE's SERDJ archive starts at vol. 17, so vol. 11 is not hosted there. The journal society site failed TLS (certificate mismatch). No abstract or full text was found.
findings.consequence: This may be a second publication of overlapping Ln D data, so it is a possible duplicate-source risk if the corpus also holds it. Check whether any corpus DOI or record matches SERDJ 11:1-10. It is not readable publicly.

findings.question: (2) Do JAEA documents restate D values for DMDPhPDA?
findings.statement: JAEA patent US8052947B2 (Yaita, Shiwaku, Suzuki, Okamoto; priority JP 2006-349646). It uses 0.5 M 'PDA' (N,N'-dimethyl-N,N'-diphenyl-2,6-pyridinedicarboxamide) in chloroform. Stated values: D(Am) 1.3 and D(Eu) 0.25 at 3.0 M HNO3; D(Pu) 10.2 at 3.0 M and 42.5 at 5.0 M; D(U) 0.17 at 3.0 M. No La, Ce, Pr or Nd values, no 5 M Ln values, and no stated SF.
findings.consequence: This gives one independent Eu D point (0.25 at 3 M HNO3, 0.5 M ligand, CHCl3) to cross-check the corpus's Eu value under matching conditions. It cannot check Pr/Nd at 5 M.

findings.question: (2) Do later Shimada/Yaita papers on DMDPhPDA restate the 5 M Pr/Nd D or SF?
findings.statement: Fujiwara (née Shimada), Nakano, Yaita, Okuno, J. Alloys Compd. 456 (2008) 429-435, is a structural/stability-constant study. OpenAlex has no abstract and its keywords are structural only. Yaita et al., Physica Scripta T115 (2005) 302, is an XAFS study of Ce-DMDPhPDA in methanol and showed no extraction data. JAEA AESJ abstracts by Arisaka/Watanabe/Kimura (2007-2010) cover alkyl-PDA adsorbents for Am/Eu, which is a different ligand. None of these states the Pr or Nd D at 5 M or an SF Pr/Nd.
findings.consequence: No later restatement was found to arbitrate the decade discrepancy.

findings.question: (3) Anything stating separation behaviour along the Ln series for this system
findings.statement: An IJMS 2022 open-access paper (PMC9779341) cites Shimada 2004 as ref. [10]. It states that for pyridine-2,6-dicarboxylic acid diamides 'positive sequences D vs. Z are observed', i.e. D rises from La toward Lu. It gives no numeric D or SF for the Shimada system.
findings.consequence: This supports the sign only: D(Nd) > D(Pr), so SF Nd/Pr > 1, for this system. It gives no magnitude, so it cannot pick the decade. If one corpus copy implies D(Pr) > D(Nd) at 5 M, that copy conflicts with this secondary statement.

findings.question: (3) Any stated numeric separation factors along the series (e.g., SF Pr/Nd) for DMDPhPDA
findings.statement: No public page stated a numeric adjacent-Ln SF for DMDPhPDA. Several open-access citing works could not be read: the Energies 2022 review (MDPI, HTTP 403), the EJIC 2024 review (Wiley, 403) and JNST 2014 (T&F, 403). The Alyapyshev/Babain/Paulenova dipicolinamide abstracts (2008, 2011) give Am/Ln only, with no Ln/Ln SF.
findings.consequence: No external number exists to replace or validate the corpus SF Pr/Nd at 5 M. Treat the pair as unresolved, or apply a provenance rule, until the thesis is read.

findings.question: (1) OSTI/INIS records with full text
findings.statement: OSTI/ETDEWEB has a record (biblio 21130093) for the 2008 structural DMDPhPDA paper, but the OSTI host refused connections (ECONNREFUSED). INIS search and API returned HTTP 402 (Payment Required), which I did not pursue. JAEA's JOPSS search returned empty pages (JS-driven).
findings.consequence: I could not check whether an INIS/OSTI full text exists. This is a low-probability source for the SEIX Table 1, since the main lead is the Shizuoka thesis.

summary:
No public page states the Pr or Nd D at 5 M HNO3, or an SF Pr/Nd, for DMDPhPDA. The one-decade discrepancy cannot be resolved from accessible sources yet.

Verified from source:
(a) The SEIX abstract (via OpenAlex; the T&F page returned 403) has no numbers. It says acid concentration drives the inter-Ln differences. The paper is closed access.
(b) An AESJ 2003 fall-meeting abstract by Shimada/Yaita/Okuno/Kimura says D rises sharply above about 3 M HNO3, especially for heavy Ln. A one-decade slip at 5 M is therefore chemically plausible either way.
(c) A JAEA patent, US8052947B2, gives an independent Eu cross-check point: 0.5 M ligand in CHCl3, 3.0 M HNO3, D(Eu) = 0.25 and D(Am) = 1.3. It has no Pr or Nd values.

Secondary: IJMS 2022 (PMC9779341) cites the paper for a 'positive sequence' of D vs Z. This implies D(Nd) > D(Pr), i.e. SF Nd/Pr > 1, as a sign check only.

The key lead: Shimada's 2004 Shizuoka University PhD thesis (DOI 10.14945/00003509) is open access as K0379.pdf (23.8 MB, Japanese). It very likely contains the original Ln D data. I did not download it, per the task rules. Reading it needs explicit user permission and possibly OCR.

There is also a companion paper with the same authors: SERDJ vol. 11 (2004) pp. 1-10, on Am(III) and Ln(III) with DMDPhPDA. It is not online (J-STAGE starts at vol. 17) and may duplicate the D data, so check the corpus for it.

OSTI was unreachable, INIS returned HTTP 402, and the MDPI, Wiley and T&F full texts returned 403.

Side effect: one WebFetch of a J-STAGE PDF (the Ozawa et al. 2010 SERDJ 17:19 review) was saved automatically by the tool to C:\Users\Bandai\.claude\projects\D--ml-separator-gh\0cd609d3-ed34-4de3-83c3-904e5f4bdb8b\tool-results\webfetch-1792688655177-twcwe9.pdf (1.1 MB). It was not opened or used. Its public abstract mentions PDA only for An/Ln separation, with no Pr/Nd.

Elsewhere it defines a positive sequence as D increasing "in the series from La to Lu". So "D rises from La toward Lu" is the article's own definition, and the claim is accurate. topic: New, independent full lanthanide-series extraction data (training or confirmation candidates): D4GC01146E, SAFE database, and recent open-access Ln-series D sources

findings.question: What is Green Chemistry DOI 10.1039/D4GC01146E (title, authors, venue, licence)?
findings.statement: Crossref metadata gives the title 'Agile synthesis and automated, high-throughput evaluation of diglycolamides for liquid–liquid extraction of rare-earth elements'. Authors: Lun An, Yue Yao, Tyler B. Hall, Fu Zhao, Long Qi. Published in Green Chem. 26(12), 7188–7197. Licence CC BY-NC 3.0 from 22 May 2024. OpenAlex lists it as hybrid OA and records an OSTI copy (biblio 2352801, submitted version). The deposited abstract is generic: it names no metals and no conditions.
findings.consequence: Identity confirmed. The open licence means its ESI tables can be reused, but the metadata alone does not settle what conditions it reports.

findings.question: Which extractants and conditions does D4GC01146E use?
findings.statement: The Ames Lab CMI highlight confirms 'over 180 runs in 48 hours' and separation of 'light and heavy REEs'. Search-engine summaries, not read from the article, say nine DGAs were made by solvent-free melt amidation in 85–96% yield. No source I could read states the acid, its concentration, the diluent or the DGA concentration.
findings.consequence: The extraction conditions are still unverified from the web. Take them from the ESI tables the corpus already cites; do not infer them.

findings.question: Does the D4GC01146E article or ESI give D for a full or nearly full La–Lu series?
findings.statement: The RSC HTML, PDF and landing pages returned HTTP 403. The ESI URL is in the search index (rsc.org/suppdata/d4/gc/d4gc01146e/d4gc01146e1.pdf) but returned 404 to the fetch tool. OSTI refused the connection. In the browser pane, pubs.rsc.org showed a bot check, which I did not try to pass. Local context only, not web-verified: the corpus provenance cites Tables S15, S16, S17, S18 and S20. auxiliary_ln.csv lists 14 Ln (La–Lu, no Pm) for TODGA and for N,N'-dimethyl-N,N'-dioctyl-DGA.
findings.consequence: Whether the series is full cannot be confirmed from the web here. Locally the corpus already holds 14-Ln rows from this paper, so it is not a new independent source. Its only use would be a re-check of the transcribed ESI values (D:/ml_separator_gh/generations/gen21/round4_20261022/results/provenance/auxiliary_ln.csv).

findings.question: Is 10.1039/D4GC01146E in our corpus DOI list?
findings.statement: Yes. corpus_dois.csv has the row '10.1039/d4gc01146e,pub_4cba27f5f3,...,2024'. sources_by_doi.csv lists 8 cells, 96 c3 pairs, 5 extractants and 1 flagged cell, curated by Thomas Summers.
findings.consequence: It is not new data. RESEARCH_IDEAS.md item 3 frames it as a 'genuinely new matched-series source', which is wrong: the publication is already in the cohort.

findings.question: What does the SAFE documentation say about access (login?)
findings.statement: The /doc page says 'You need to sign up to use our database.' Users log in, browse, and download what they select with a 'Download as CSV' button. Uploads need PI or admin approval. The homepage still calls SAFE 'a centralized, publicly accessible database'. The public pages mention no API and no data licence; /terms returned 404.
findings.consequence: Data access needs an account, and the project rules forbid logging in. SAFE stays out of reach unless the user exports the CSV.

findings.question: What record types does SAFE hold, and does it state counts of lanthanide extraction records?
findings.statement: On 2026-10-22 the homepage showed Metals 41, Extractants 324, Records 18388, Users 228, Downloads 4941. It describes 'experimental and computational data' covering liquid–liquid extraction and solid–liquid chromatography. Featured metals include Eu, Ce, Nd, Pr, Am and Cm, and featured extractants include TODGA, Me2-TODGA, TEHDGA and DEHPA. No public page gives a lanthanide-specific record count or a field list (D, SF, conditions). An older search-index snapshot showed 39 metals, 52 extractants and 8,716 records, so the database has roughly doubled.
findings.consequence: The lanthanide record count is not stated anywhere public (NOT FOUND). SAFE may hold Me2-TODGA and other DGA series that overlap the corpus, and how much overlaps cannot be judged without logging in.

findings.question: Is the SAFE description paper open?
findings.statement: The paper is Silva Garcia Leite et al., 'Creation of the Separation Archive for Elements (SAFE) Database', Solvent Extr. Ion Exch. 43(7), 847–852 (2025). It is a short letter to the editors. OpenAlex marks it closed, with no licence, and Taylor & Francis returned 403.
findings.consequence: There is no open documentation of SAFE's schema or provenance per record. Treat any SAFE export as having unknown overlap with the corpus until it is checked DOI by DOI.

findings.question: Candidate: 14-Ln N-heterocycle data set with numeric D
findings.statement: Gerasimov et al., Molecules 29 (2024) 3548, DOI 10.3390/molecules29153548, CC BY 4.0. The ligand is a 4,7-dichloro-phenanthroline-2,9-diamide (N,N'-diethyl-N,N'-di(p-hexylphenyl)), a tetradentate N,O DAPhen. It reports 14 Ln (La–Lu, no Pm) plus Am. Conditions: 3 M HNO3, 0.025 M ligand, 298 K, eight diluents (toluene, F-3, nitrobenzene, CHCl3, DCE, 1-octanol, 1-dodecanol, C4mimNTf2). Numeric Ln D values are in SI Table S3. Not in the corpus.
findings.consequence: This is the strongest confirmation candidate: a non-DGA class, a full series, numeric values, and several diluents at fixed acid, which isolates the diluent effect. Before use, check author or ligand overlap with the corpus phenanthroline-diamide papers (10.1039/d0ra05182a, 10.1021/acs.inorgchem.1c01729).

findings.question: Candidate: fluorinated or chlorinated pyrrolidine phenanthroline diamides
findings.statement: IJMS 24 (2023) 5569, DOI 10.3390/ijms24065569, CC BY 4.0. Extraction was studied for 'lanthanides(III) (except for Pm(III))' with L2 (4,7-Cl2) and L3 (4,7-F2) pyrrolidine phenanthroline diamides. Conditions: 5 M HNO3, 0.01 M ligand (L3 also 0.05 M at 3 and 5 M HNO3), diluent F-3 (3-nitrobenzotrifluoride). Ln D values are plotted only (Fig. 8b,c), and no temperature is stated for the extractions. Not in the corpus.
findings.consequence: Two paired ligands differ only by Cl versus F at 4,7, a clean electronic-substituent contrast. The values would have to be digitised from plots (reliability caveat). The 14-element list is implied by the text, not enumerated.

findings.question: Candidate: phenanthroline-2,9-diamides L2–L5 (tetrabutyl, dichloro, pyrrolidine variants)
findings.statement: Ustynyuk et al., IJMS 23 (2022) 15538, DOI 10.3390/ijms232415538, CC BY 4.0. It reports V-shaped D-versus-Z curves 'from La to Lu' with a minimum at Gd. Conditions: 3 M HNO3 (5 M in Fig. 2b), F-3 and F-3/p-xylene mixtures, 25 °C. Ligand concentration is inconsistent: 0.7 M in Methods, 0.5 M in the Fig. 2 captions. The text says D values are given in the Supplementary Materials. Not in the corpus.
findings.consequence: Possibly four ligands times a full series. The exact Ln count and the SI table were not seen, and the concentration discrepancy must be resolved before use.

findings.question: Candidate: bis-lactam phenanthroline (BLPhen) in a hydrocarbon diluent
findings.statement: Karslyan et al., RSC Adv. 9 (2019) 26537, DOI 10.1039/c9ra06115k, CC BY (Europe PMC). Ligand: BLPhen with 2-octyldecyl chains. It reports 14 Ln plus Y (Fig. 2c). Conditions: 3 M HNO3, 0.3 mM of each metal, 4 mM ligand, Isopar L with 10 vol% Exxal 13, 25 °C. Values are plotted only; ESI Table SI-4 holds Eu data. Not in the corpus, which has the earlier BLPhen paper 10.1002/chem.201806443.
findings.consequence: A light-selective N-heterocycle series under conditions independent of the corpus paper. It needs digitising. It shares a ligand family with a corpus paper, so it should be held out by family, not as an unrelated extractant.

findings.question: Candidate: isomeric (N-alkyl) DGAs with a numeric 14-Ln table
findings.statement: Liu et al., RSC Adv. 12 (2022, online 24 Dec 2021) 790, DOI 10.1039/d1ra07020g, CC BY-NC (Europe PMC). Ligands: L^II = N,N-dimethyl-N',N'-dioctyl DGA and L^I = N,N'-dimethyl-N,N'-dioctyl DGA. Table 1 gives numeric D for all 14 Ln at 3 M HNO3 in 40/60 n-octanol/kerosene; the L^I values come from the authors' earlier study (ref. 16). These are N-alkyl isomers, not alpha-substituted. Not in the corpus.
findings.consequence: The L^II series is new. The L^I series probably repeats corpus DOI 10.1007/s10967-020-07242-1 (same ligand, '14 lanthanides', 2020), which must be checked before counting it. This is a DGA class, not the preferred non-DGA.

findings.question: Candidate: quaternary phosphonium nitrate (basic extractant), La–Lu
findings.statement: Onghena et al. (KU Leuven), RSC Adv. 8 (2018) 32044, DOI 10.1039/c8ra06712k, CC BY-NC (Europe PMC). The extractant is undiluted [P66614][NO3]. D was measured from La (Z=57) to Lu (Z=71) without Pm, at several NH4NO3 concentrations, 0.01 M Ln feed, A/O 1:1, 70 °C. Values are plotted only (Fig. 2). Not in the corpus.
findings.consequence: A non-DGA class with an opposite chemistry (anion exchange). Undiluted extractant and 70 °C are far outside the corpus domain, so it suits an out-of-domain stress test better than training. Needs digitising.

findings.question: Candidate: HDEHP into an ionic liquid, 14 Ln
findings.statement: Matsutani & Katsuta, Solvent Extr. Res. Dev. Jpn. 30(2) (2023) 121–128, DOI 10.15261/serdj.30.121, J-STAGE 'Journal Free Access'. The abstract covers 14 trivalent lanthanoids with HDEHP in [C4mim][Tf2N] against toluene, as a function of pH and HDEHP concentration. It notes 'a shaking time of more than 36 hours is needed'. From the landing page, the acid, concentrations, temperature and whether D is tabulated could not be read. Not in the corpus.
findings.consequence: Two diluents with the same extractant across the full series, from an acidic organophosphorus class the corpus lacks. Full text is free, but only as a PDF, which I did not read.

findings.question: Candidates whose Ln count or conditions could not be verified (Dalton 2026 BLPhen; Anal. Sci. 2020 TDdPTDA)
findings.statement: Gao, Fang & Xiao, Dalton Trans. 55 (2026) 5679, DOI 10.1039/d5dt03012a, CC BY-NC hybrid OA. The abstract covers four BLPhen alkyl-amide variants and light, middle and heavy Ln stoichiometries; the RSC full text returned 403. Tsutsui et al., Anal. Sci. 36 (2020) 241, DOI 10.2116/analsci.19P275, free access. That paper uses tetradodecyl-phenanthroline-2,9-diamide in F-3, nitrobenzene or n-dodecane, and its landing page does not give the Ln count. Neither is in the corpus.
findings.consequence: Both are plausible N-heterocycle series, but neither is confirmed to have 10 or more Ln with stated D. Check them manually in a browser before relying on them.

findings.question: Checked and excluded (fewer than 10 Ln with D, or no D)
findings.statement: Excluded after reading the text: Molecules 27 (2022) 1786, BTPhen, Eu only. ACS Omega 2019 (10.1021/acsomega.9b03241), HDEHDGA, La–Nd only. Molecules 30 (2025) 786, pyrazolone + phen/bipy, La/Eu/Lu only. ACS Cent. Sci. 2018 (10.1021/acscentsci.8b00223), 4 new Ln. RSC Adv. 2025 (10.1039/d5ra00815h), UDGAs, at most 3 Ln measurable. Fundam. Res. 2023 (10.1016/j.fmre.2023.01.004), DFT only, no D. Molecules 31 (2026) 656, pyrazolone-N-heterocycle chelators, gives % extraction for 'all rare earths, excluding the radioactive Pm' but not D. Inorg. Chem. Front. 2025 (10.1039/d5qi01056j), the abstract mentions only Eu among Ln.
findings.consequence: These do not qualify as 10-or-more-Ln D series. Molecules 31:656 could give % extraction but would need a phase-ratio conversion, which is not to be inferred.

findings.question: Open-access alpha-substituted DGA full-series data, and Zenodo/figshare data sets
findings.statement: No open-access 2018–2026 source found with D for 10 or more Ln with an alpha-substituted (backbone-methylated) DGA. The Me-TODGA and mTDDGA hits were either in closed SEIX papers or gave Am/Cm-only tables (NJC 2023, which is corpus DOI d2nj05663a). Keyword searches through the Zenodo and figshare APIs returned only unrelated records, so no open data set of Ln distribution ratios was found.
findings.consequence: No new open alpha-DGA confirmation series is available. The alpha-DGA arm would rely on corpus 10.1002/chem.201806161 and 10.1039/d2nj05663a, or on SAFE (login required).
